newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Dow gains seen hitting foreign interest in Colombo.
newsitem.headline: Dow gains seen hitting foreign interest in Colombo.

text.p: Sharp gains on Wall Street are likely to hit foreign interest on the Colombo Stock Exchange on Wednesday as emerging markets may lose out in the battle for funds, brokers said.

"Going purely on domestic factors, the all share should gain. But with Wall Street and a number of other foreign markets doing well, emerging markets will have to compete for funds," said Dihan Dedigama of brokerage John Keells.
Colombo stocks closed 9.42 points up at 727.32 on Tuesday on turnover of 210.2 million rupees.
But brokers also said local buying should maintain the market at healthy levels even if foreign interest dips due to global funds looking away from emerging markets.
The all share lost nearly four percent between April 23-25 as the market began a correction after rising more than 15 percent in the previous six weeks.
"Even the blue chips are looking good again after the correction," said Ajit Wanigasekera of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Turnover is expected to be at previous levels on Wednesday on active buying of pricey blue chips and low-valued shares, brokers said.
